chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When one of you intends to marry, what does he do?' I said, 'I do not know.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he intends that, let him pray two Rak'at, and praise Allah, then let him say:'

O Allah! I intend to marry, so ordain for me from the women the one who is most chaste in her private part, and most protective of me regarding herself and my wealth, and one of extensive sustenance, and the greatest of blessings; and ordain for me a good child, making him a righteous successor during my life and after my death.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer and supplication for a man before marriage in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) via the chain of Abu Basir, emphasizing the spiritual preparation for marriage through a specific two-rak'ah prayer. The supplication highlights key Shia ethical priorities: selecting a spouse who is chaste ('afafan), protective of the husband's honor and wealth, and blessed with sustenance, ultimately seeking offspring who serve as a righteous legacy (khala salih) in life and after death. This ritual underscores the transition of marital intimacy from mere physical desire to a divinely ordained act of worship and continuity of faith.
